punchline: Write so many goals that you run out of the ones you're supposed to want and find the ones you actually want.
thirty_sec: In The Power of Focus, Jack Canfield, Mark Victor Hansen and Les Hewitt argue that goals you keep only in your head tend to stay wishes. One exercise linked to them is writing a long list, around 101 goals, without asking whether each is realistic. Writing turns a wish into a commitment. And once the obvious goals run out, the deeper ones you really care about start to appear.
question: Is the goal that matters most to you this year written down anywhere, or does it only live in your head?
